We don't know how she will fare in her American tennis tournaments, if she participates in any following her return to this country, but on the basis of her play in England alone she gets the first-rank today.

Her victory over Helen Jacobs, to be sure, was one-sided and might not have been achieved with such ease had the latter not aggravated an ankle injury early in the second set. Nevertheless Mrs. Moody conquered the very best players in the feminine tennis world. She also achieved something that no other player before her did. She is an eight-time winner at Wimbledon. This stretch of victories began back in 1927, which is 11 years ago.

All praise then to Mrs. Moody and certainly to red-headed Budge, three-times winner this year at historic Wimbledon. It was America's year to rule the English courts. And might we point out that 1938 seems destined to restore fully and completely the domination of international tennis that the United States once maintained undisputed. How long it will last, we don't know, but while we have it, let's enjoy it.
